papers.title: Discovery of Singularities in Partial Differential Equations Using Adaptive Numerical Discretizations
papers.abstract: We compute self-similar singularity profiles of partial differential equations (PDEs) using adaptive numerical discretizations based on optimizing a discrete loss (ODIL). The fields are represented in overlapping local Chebyshev patches joined with a mapped asymptotic patch. After factoring out the leading power laws of solution ansatzes, their limiting amplitudes at infinity are determined by the optimization, eliminating domain truncation and prescribed far-field conditions. Adaptive refinement is guided by Chebyshev-coefficient decay, and the nonlinear least-squares problem is solved using automatically differentiated Gauss--Newton iterations with Levenberg--Marquardt damping. The method achieves O(10^{-14})-level accuracy for Burgers profiles, residuals of O(10^{-14}) to O(10^{-10}) for the generalized De Gregorio family, and of O(10^{-8}) in a local region for the two-dimensional Boussinesq equations. These results demonstrate that ODIL can identify singularity profiles for PDEs with high accuracy using adaptive numerical methods, complementing ongoing efforts that rely on artificial intelligence.

papers.title: Entropy bounded compact stencil Runge-Kutta discontinuous Galerkin method for hyperbolic conservation laws
papers.abstract: In this paper we introduce a compact stencil Runge-Kutta discontinuous Galerkin method for the Euler equations of compressible gas dynamics, which preserves a minimum entropy principle similar to that introduced by Tadmor for entropy solution of the Euler equations [4]. Compact stencil RKDG, introduced by Chen et al. in [15], is a variant of standard RKDG method which is known for its smaller stencil size and parallel efficiency. The main challenge is that the cRKDG method has to be expressed in Butcher form and not every Runge-Kutta method of this form is a convex combination of forward-Euler steps. Therefore, in order to establish this property we leverage the bound preserving framework of the cRKDG schemes [8], an entropy bounded limiter [6] and the classical positivity preserving limiter. In the last section numerical experiments are provided to demonstrate the robustness of the method.

papers.title: Numerical reconstruction of polygonal obstacles by diffracted waves
papers.abstract: We present a numerical method for recovering rigid polygonal obstacles in two dimensions, based on the diffraction-based inverse scattering theory of Bao, Chen, Lu, and Xiong. A single pulse is emitted from a point source, and the resulting wave field is measured on a receiver curve. After isolating the diffracted signals, we recover the visible vertices from arrival times and the corner orientations and opening angles from amplitudes. The use of amplitude information permits local reconstruction in the reflection shadow, where reflected waves do not reach the receiver. The amplitudes also determine the direction of a shadowed edge adjacent to a visible vertex, enabling local non-line-of-sight imaging. Numerical experiments for a convex corner, a concave corner, a triangle, a pentagon and a star-shaped obstacle confirm that the visible portion of the boundary can be recovered stably from diffracted signals. A further convex-corner test with additive noise at level $0.2\%$ on the single arc $L_1$ confirms that the tip and opening remain recoverable.

papers.title: Global well-posedness for the modified dispersion-generalized Benjamin-Ono equations
papers.abstract: In this short note, we prove the global well-posedness of the modified dispersion-generalized Benjamin-Ono equation with dispersion $1<\alpha<2$, $$\partial_t u + D^\alpha \partial_x u + u^2\partial_x u=0,$$ over the Sobolev space $H^s(\mathbb{R})$, for any regularity $s$ greater or equal than the sharp analytic well-posedness regularity. As a byproduct, we also derive nonlinear smoothing estimates and give a simple proof of local well-posedness.

papers.title: Scattering of plane waves and a modified Pompeiu criterion
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove that plane waves always scatter from bounded, strictly convex planar inhomogeneities with constant material parameters. Our approach involves the introduction of a modified Pompeiu property, whose failure corresponds to the vanishing of the Fourier transform of the indicator function of the inhomogeneity on a complexified circle not centered at the origin. We then show that such vanishing is impossible for bounded, strictly convex planar sets.

papers.title: Finite time implosions of the multidimensional compressible Euler equations with a finite far-field cutoff
papers.abstract: We study the problem of finite time singularities in the isentropic compressible Euler equations in multiple dimensions with radial symmetry. Our initial data consists of the radially symmetric Kidder self-similar implosion with a continuous constant density cutoff. Motivated by our recent work on the one-dimensional problem, we present high-resolution radially symmetric adaptive mesh refinement simulations that when combined with asymptotic similarity solution analysis present a full picture of the ensuing dynamics of the implosion. From the cutoff point in the initial data, an expanding wave emerges. The endpoints of the wave follow the "imploding" and "exploding" characteristic speeds associated with the system of hyperbolic conservation laws. This wave has much more complex structure than the exact non-centered rarefaction wave that emerges in the one-dimensional problem. As in the one-dimensional case, the inner Kidder solution is swallowed up by the expanding wave as time approaches the singularity time. However, unlike the one-dimensional case, a blowup occurs along the point where the `imploding' side of the expanding wave attaches to the Kidder solution. This composite blowup has an asymptotic self-similar form that has an interpretation in terms of the Gurderley-type self-similarity structure. The numerical method for the PDE necessitates a Lagrangian scheme to avoid the numerical diffusion inherent in Eulerian methods. We use a leapfrog method coupled to recursive refinement of the mesh near the blowup, which allows for very high resolution simulations, resolving many orders of magnitude of the self-similar blowup. Consistent with prior rigorous results for these equations, the blowup does not involve mass concentration and exhibits a critical $L^p$ space for the concentration of the density, depending on the dimension of space.

papers.title: The Porous Medium Equation and Convexity
papers.abstract: We show that root convexity of the pressure is preserved by the porous medium equation if the initial data is root convex, positive, smooth, bounded below by a quadratic function and has bounded Laplacian. This complements a result of Daskalopoulos-Hamilton-Lee on root concavity of pressure.

papers.title: Source integrability and the frontier $\alpha=\tfrac12$ in time-fractional diffusion
papers.abstract: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{d}$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain, let $\alpha\in(0,1)$, and let $\partial_{t}^{\alpha}$ denote the Caputo derivative. For $\partial_{t}^{\alpha}u-\nabla\cdot\bigl(A(x)\nabla u\bigr)=f$ with homogeneous Dirichlet condition and initial datum $g\in L^{2}(\Omega)$, we identify which of the thresholds appearing in the energy method belong to the method and which to the equation. We compare $f\in L^{2}\bigl((0,T);L^{2}(\Omega)\bigr)$ and $f\in L^{r}\bigl((0,T);L^{2}(\Omega)\bigr)$ with $r>2/\alpha$; in the subdiffusive range the second implies the first and not conversely. Existence is not at issue and we claim none of it: it is known, for both hypotheses and under weaker ones, from the work of Zacher. What we determine is the exact set of exponents each route admits and what the exponents left outside it cost. Under the weaker hypothesis the construction below reaches $\alpha\in(\frac12,1)$, under the stronger one every $\alpha\in(0,1)$, and in both cases the solution lies in $L^{\infty}\bigl((0,T);L^{2}(\Omega)\bigr)$, by the mode representation and not by the energy route, which yields no such bound under the weaker hypothesis. The restriction $\alpha>\frac12$ comes from the compactness criterion, whose admissible exponents form $[1,2\alpha)$; the exponent $r>2/\alpha$ is exactly what the Gr\"onwall step consumes. A concentrating family shows that nothing weaker suffices along that route, and the mode representation lowers the requirement to $1/\alpha$. The frontier $\alpha=\frac12$ belongs to the equation: for every $\alpha\in(0,\frac12]$ there is $f\in L^{2}\bigl((0,T);L^{2}(\Omega)\bigr)$ whose weak solution leaves $L^{\infty}\bigl((0,T);L^{2}(\Omega)\bigr)$. Uniqueness and Hadamard well-posedness follow.

papers.title: The Serrin exponent for Lane-Emden inequalities driven by sums of fractional p-Laplacians
papers.abstract: We study positive weak super-solutions of the Lane-Emden inequality $\mathcal{L}u := \sum_{i=1}^{n}(-\Delta_{p_i})^{s_i}u \ge u^q$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$, where each $(-\Delta_{p_i})^{s_i}$ is a fractional $p_i$-Laplacian of order $s_i\in(0,1]$ and exponent $p_i\in(1,\infty)$, and $\max_i s_ip_i<N$. Let $\kappa_i := (N-s_ip_i)/(p_i-1)$ be the decay exponent of the fundamental solution of the $i$-th operator, and let $\overline{\kappa} := \max_i\kappa_i$. We show that the Serrin exponent of $\mathcal{L}$ is $\mathfrak{q}_{\mathcal{L}} = N/\overline{\kappa}$. More precisely, for $0<q<\mathfrak{q}_{\mathcal{L}}$ the only non-negative continuous weak super-solution is $u\equiv 0$, while for every $q>\mathfrak{q}_{\mathcal{L}}$ we construct explicit positive weak super-solutions of the form $A(\lambda+|x|)^{-\kappa}$. In other words, the Serrin exponent of the sum is the smallest of the Serrin exponents $N/\kappa_i$ of the single operators, that is, the one of the operator whose fundamental solution decays fastest. No structural assumption relating the different operators is needed. The endpoint $q=\mathfrak{q}_{\mathcal{L}}$ is left open. The local order $s_i=1$ is treated together with the nonlocal orders, and all the arguments are carried out in the weak setting.

papers.title: Supercritical magnetic ray transforms in hyperbolic space: the complexification method from the transport-twistor lens
papers.abstract: We present new inversion formulas for the unattenuated and attenuated magnetic ray transforms in the Poincar\'e disk, in the case of a constant, supercritical magnetic field. Our approach mirrors earlier complexification approaches by Novikov (Ark. Mat., 2002) and Bal (J. Math. Pures Appl., 2005), and a second feature of this article is to connect the approach with the Transport Twistor framework recently introduced by Bohr-Paternain (J. \'Ec. polytech. Math., 2023; arXiv:2606.25173).

papers.title: Scattering theory for bulk and surface waves in an impedance half-space, II: local perturbations, the scattering matrix and an inverse problem
papers.abstract: We study the Robin, or impedance, Laplacian on a half-space of dimension $n \ge 3$ which is perturbed inside a fixed ball. The boundary may be deformed, and obstacles may be present in the interior or attached to the boundary, in any combination and with no smallness assumption. Outside the ball the configuration is the flat impedance half-space of Part I, with constant impedance $\alpha > 0$, where a bulk channel and a surface channel propagate at every positive energy and only the surface channel propagates on the band $(-\alpha^2,0)$. We prove a limiting absorption principle, valid at every positive energy and outside a discrete set of embedded eigenvalues in the band. We construct the generalized Fourier transform and prove its completeness by a stationary argument which constructs no wave operator and reduces completeness to the uniqueness of the scattering solution at each energy. We then obtain the scattering matrix, its unitarity and a two-channel optical theorem. The main result is a uniqueness theorem for the inverse problem. Under two geometric conditions on the pair, the scattering amplitude at a single positive energy determines the perturbation completely, and the argument does not distinguish a deformation of the boundary from an obstacle. It follows that no nontrivial perturbation satisfying the same conditions is invisible at any positive energy. On the surface band the corresponding statement is reduced to one explicitly stated question about the exterior Robin problem.

papers.title: Non-Uniqueness of Weak Solutions to the Unforced Two-Dimensional Euler Equations with Vorticity in $L^1\cap L^p$, Part I: A Compactness Criterion and the Linear Analysis
papers.abstract: This paper and its companion Part II prove that the incompressible Euler equations in the plane, without external force, admit two distinct renormalized weak solutions with the same initial vorticity $f$, where $f$ is radial and nonnegative and lies in $(L^1\cap L^q)(\mathbb{R}^2)$ for every $q<\infty$ but is not bounded. One solution is radially symmetric and stationary. The other is $3$-fold rotationally symmetric, is equimeasurable with $f$ at every time, and departs from $f$ in finite time; the two solutions are distinct in $L^\infty_t(L^1\cap L^q)_x$ on $[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^2$ for every $q\in(4/3,\infty)$ and every sufficiently large $T$. In this first part we prove two ingredients. One is a compactness criterion: for a radial datum, a sequence of $3$-fold rotationally symmetric solutions with converging data, whose non-radial moment is bounded below at some bounded time, has a subsequence converging to a second distinct renormalized weak solution. The other is the linear analysis for the building blocks of our multiscale datum. We show that the linearization of the Euler equations around the basic building block plus a small point vortex has an unstable eigenvalue in a space of $3$-fold rotationally symmetric perturbations. This latter argument depends on rigorous interval arithmetic that we discuss more fully in Part II.

papers.title: Whole-space eventual log-concavity and level-set geometry for the multidimensional Fisher-KPP equation
papers.abstract: We study eventual strict log-concavity and level-set geometry for the multidimensional Fisher-KPP equation with nontrivial, nonnegative, smooth compactly supported initial data, without assuming radial symmetry or convexity of the initial superlevel sets. Our main result is that there exist $T>1$ and $c>0$ such that $D_x^2\log u(t,x)\le -(c/t)e^{-\beta_*t}\mathrm{Id}$ for all $t\ge T$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}^N$, where $\beta_*=2(\sqrt2-1)$. Consequently, after a single waiting time, $u(t,\cdot)$ has exactly one critical point, a nondegenerate global maximizer, and every level set $\{u(t,\cdot)=\lambda\}$ with $0<\lambda<\max_x u(t,x)$ is a smooth closed strictly convex hypersurface with positive principal curvatures. For levels in any fixed closed interval $K\subset(0,1)$, the level sets are radial graphs $\rho=R_\lambda(t,\omega)$, with every principal curvature bounded below by $(1-C\log t/t)/(2t)$ for all sufficiently large $t$. Unlike log-concavity, ordinary concavity exhibits a threshold determined by the inflection level of the critical travelling wave: for each fixed level above it, $u$ is eventually strictly concave on its superlevel set, whereas below it concavity eventually fails. Our proof proceeds by establishing estimates in four overlapping spatial regions. In the fixed-front region, we combine a one-sided estimate for second angular derivatives with radial and mixed derivative bounds to obtain curvature control without differentiating the Lipschitz directional phase. In the remaining regions, absorptive comparison in the invaded interior, leading-edge barriers and blow-up arguments through the diffusive scale, and Gaussian amplitude estimates combined with parabolic regularity in the exterior yield the required logarithmic-Hessian bounds.

papers.title: Weyl chambers, asymptotic expansions, and blowup analysis of explicit Toda solutions
papers.abstract: Blowup analysis is a central part of geometric analysis, and systems of PDEs such as Toda systems exhibit particularly rich blowup behavior. In [Nie25], the author constructed explicit families of radial Toda solutions whose blowup masses correspond to arbitrary elements of the Weyl group of the underlying Lie algebra. In this paper, we study these families within the framework of blowup analysis developed by C.-S. Lin and his coauthors. The key is an asymptotic analysis of the solution family that distinguishes Cartan elements in the interior of a Weyl chamber from those lying on its boundary faces. We prove a uniform upper bound for $u_i^{\lambda,H}(r)+2\log r$, so that the selection estimate holds with the center at the origin. We show that the successive bubbling scales for slow decay are determined by the intersections of the ray $H+tq_\mu$ with root hyperplanes. At each crossing, rescaling and the face asymptotics identify the limiting profiles as explicit solutions of the corresponding Levi-Toda subsystems. The masses of these successive bubbles, computed using [KLNW24], account for the entire blowup mass. Examples in type $A_2$ demonstrate this identification and exhibit both separated scalar bubbles and a simultaneous full-system bubble.

papers.title: Hasegawa-Mima equation as limit of a magnetized pressureless Euler-Boltzmann system
papers.abstract: We prove that the Hasegawa-Mima equation (HME) is the limit of a magnetized pressureless Euler-Boltzmann system in a special scaling regime. The proof relies on the derivation of a uniform estimate independent of the scaling parameter, using the particular structure of the singular system and the identification of a combination of the unknowns that compensates for fast oscillations in time. We also show that HME allow us to investigate a conditional property of inverse energy cascade and drift waves.

papers.title: Spatial Decay and Asymptotic Stability of Forced Waves at the Critical Speed for the Fisher-KPP Equation in a Shifting Environment
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the spatial decay and asymptotic stability of forced waves for the Fisher-KPP equation in a shifting heterogeneous environment, focusing on the critical speed $c_*=2\sqrt{r_+}$. Within the framework of regular variation, we establish a complete classification of critical wave tails in terms of the asymptotic behavior of the environmental deviation $r_+-r(z)$ as $z\to+\infty$. In each case, we derive precise spatial decay that characterize how the environmental tail modifies the leading-order decay of the wave at criticality. We further establish asymptotic stability estimates of forced waves. For initial data satisfying an exponentially weighted boundedness condition, we prove an $O(t^{-1/2})$ convergence rate in the uniform norm. Under stronger spatial decay assumptions on the weighted initial data, this rate improves to $O(t^{-1-\sigma/2})$, for $\sigma\in[0,1]$, in both the uniform norm and a weighted norm. Moreover, no smallness assumption on the initial perturbations is needed for our results.

papers.title: Global well-posedness and Newtonian limit of the compressible upper-convected Maxwell model in analytic spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the compressible upper-convected Maxwell (UCM) system in \(\mathbb{R}^3\), which corresponds to the purely elastic case of the compressible Oldroyd-B model with vanishing retardation time. In this regime, the velocity equation loses the viscous dissipation term, and the constitutive nonlinearities induce a derivative loss, so that the standard approaches in Sobolev or finitely regular Besov spaces fail. We therefore work in analytic function spaces, realized as exponentially weighted hybrid Besov spaces, and develop a global-in-time analytic framework based on Littlewood--Paley analysis and uniform-in-\(\tau\) energy estimates. A key ingredient is the introduction of the kinematic stress tensor, which allows us to establish the required a priori estimates in hybrid Besov spaces. Based on these estimates, we prove the existence of a unique global-in-time analytic solution for small analytic initial data. Moreover, for ill-prepared data, we rigorously justify the global-in-time relaxation (Newtonian) limit as the relaxation parameter \(\tau\to0\), with an explicit convergence rate of order \(O(\sqrt{\tau})\).

papers.title: Nonlocal Fisher--KPP propagation with heavy tails
papers.abstract: We study a nonlocal Fisher--KPP equation on the real line with compactly supported initial data. The reaction satisfies $f(s)\le f^{\prime}(0)s$ for $0\le s\le1$, with a power bound on $f^{\prime}(0)s-f(s)$ near zero. For continuous even probability kernels $J$ comparable to $|x|^{-\gamma}$, $\gamma>1$, we prove a global two-sided estimate and locate every fixed level set with a bounded error in $\log|x|$. The propagation scale is $\exp(f'(0)t/\gamma)$ for every $\gamma>1$. This differs sharply from the free-boundary propagation studied by Du and Ni \cite{DuNiJEMS}. For polynomial kernel tails, spreading in their model has linear, algebraic or $t\log t$ growth. We also obtain arrival-time and weighted-integral estimates and identify a spatial tail coefficient when $|x|^\gamma J(x)$ has a positive limit.

papers.title: Initial-boundary value problems for linear lattice differential equations
papers.abstract: We study initial-boundary value problems for linear lattice differential equations on the half-line. We first give a systematic account of fundamental solutions for equations with general finite-range interactions. We then develop complementary approaches based on reflection, the Laplace transform, and the unified transform method, obtaining contour integral and Bessel-function representations of solutions. For the semidiscrete diffusion equation, we justify these representations for continuous boundary data and initial data of polynomial growth, establish uniqueness in the corresponding growth class, and derive spatial estimates and long-time properties, including asymptotic periodicity. We also treat nonhomogeneous equations, Robin boundary conditions, nonsymmetric coefficients, and a class of time-dependent coefficients. Finally, higher-order examples illustrate how the unified transform approach extends beyond second-order equations.

papers.title: A unified quantitative approach to Chiti and Kohler--Jobin inequalities
papers.abstract: We obtain two quantitative results related to classical rearrangement inequalities for the first Dirichlet eigenvalue. The first one is a quantitative version of Chiti's reverse H\"older inequality. More precisely, for every $1\le q<p<\infty$, we prove that the deficit controls, up to translations, the $L^q$ distance between a first eigenfunction of a bounded domain and the first eigenfunction of the ball having the same first eigenvalue. The second result concerns the Kohler--Jobin inequality and gives a quantitative estimate in terms of the $L^\infty\!\to L^2$ distance between the corresponding Dirichlet resolvents. In both cases, the main idea is to find a suitable superlevel set of the first eigenfunction which is almost optimal for the Faber-Krahn inequality.

papers.title: Potential estimates and improved Sobolev regularity for nonlocal fully nonlinear elliptic equations
papers.abstract: This paper investigates pointwise and oscillatory potential estimates for viscosity solutions and their gradients to a class of nonlocal fully nonlinear elliptic equations. The key ingredient of our argument is to establish precise pointwise bounds for a novel fractional sharp maximal function defined in terms of affine functions. As an immediate consequence, we prove higher order Sobolev regularity results of Calder\'{o}n-Zygmund type for such equations without imposing any global boundedness assumptions on viscosity solutions. The potential theory developed herein extends the work of Daskalopoulos-Kuusi-Mingione (Commun. Partial Differ. Equ. 39: 574-590, 2014) for fully nonlinear second order elliptic equations to the fractional fully nonlinear setting.

papers.title: A sharp isoperimetric bound for the ratio of the fifth and fourth eigenvalues of Dirichlet Laplacian
papers.abstract: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain with $n\geq2$. The well-known Payne-P\'olya-Weinberger conjecture for consecutive eigenvalue ratios asserts that $$ \frac{\lambda_{m+1}(\Omega)}{\lambda_m(\Omega)}\leq\left(\frac{j_{n / 2,1}}{j_{n / 2-1,1}}\right)^2,\quad m=1,2,3,\cdots. $$ Here, $j_{p,k}$ denotes the $k$-th positive zero of the Bessel function $J_p$, and $\lambda_j(\Omega)$ are the Dirichlet eigenvalues of $\Omega$, counted with multiplicity and ordered as $$ 0<\lambda_1(\Omega)<\lambda_2(\Omega)\leq\lambda_3(\Omega)\leq\cdots. $$ The cases $m=1,2,3$ were established by Ashbaugh and Benguria in their seminal works. In this paper, we give an affirmative answer to the Payne-P\'olya-Weinberger conjecture for $m=4$ by combining a quadratic-form identity with a Brouwer degree argument. We also extend the corresponding spectral inequality to arbitrary bounded open sets in $\mathbb{R}^n$.

papers.title: Sharp CR Beckner-Onofri inequalities under high-order holomorphic moment constraints
papers.abstract: We establish sharp Beckner--Onofri on the CR sphere $\mathbb{S}^{2N-1}\subset\mathbb C^N$, $N\ge2$, under vanishing holomorphic moments through degree $m\ge1$. The optimal coefficients are $\frac{1}{m+1}$. The function inequality admits a stronger form involving only the energy above degree $m$. We also prove a quantitative concentration estimate in the $1$-Wasserstein distance and show that every maximizing sequence has diverging energy and approaches the family of uniform measures on regular $(m+1)$-polygons. The proof combines subcritical minimization with rigidity of the constrained Euler--Lagrange equation, obtained from an exact radial energy identity and a Hardy space projection estimate. Finally, weighted ball automorphisms yield sharp inequalities without moment constraints, with scalar conformal, barycenter, and holomorphic Gram determinant corrections.

papers.title: Quantitative positivity properties of the temperature in multi-dimensional thermoviscoelastic systems
papers.abstract:
We consider the classical model for small-strain thermoviscoelastic evolution in isotropic Kelvin-Voigt materials with inertia, as given by $$ egin{cases} u_{tt} = \mu\Delta u_t + (\lambda+\mu)

abla\cdot u_t + \hat\mu\Delta u + (\hat\lambda+\hat\mu)

abla\cdot u - B
abla\Theta, \ \kappa\Theta_t = D\Delta\Theta + \mu|
abla u_t|^2 + (\lambda+\mu)|\mathrm{div}\,u_t|^2 - B\Theta\,\mathrm{div}\,u_t. \end{cases}$$ Recently, Winkler (arXiv:2602.05964) established global-in-time solvability for an initial value problem in smoothly bounded multi-dimensional domains $\Omega$ under homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions for the displacement variable $u$, and homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions for the temperature $\Theta$, allowing the heat capacity $\kappa$ to depend on $\Theta$. Moreover, it was shown there that the corresponding temperature is positive a.e. in $\Omega	imes(0,\infty)$. In the present work, we strengthen this positivity result by deriving a quantitative lower bound for $\Theta$. Our analysis applies to heat capacities $\kappa$ with power-law scaling for small arguments, precisely: either $\kappa(\xi)\sim\xi^\alpha$ for some $\alpha\ge 0$, or $\kappa(\xi)\ge\xi$, in a suitable neighborhood of $\xi=0$. Under these structural assumptions on $\kappa$, we show that for every $	au>0$ and $T>	au$ there exists $c(	au,T)>0$ such that $\Theta(x,t)\ge c(	au,T)$ for a.e. $(x,t)\in\Omega	imes(	au,T)$.

papers.title: Well-posedness of a stress-augmented Moore-Gibson-Thompson-type model for thermoviscoelastic evolution in a standard linear solid
papers.abstract: This manuscript studies a coupled system of nonlinear parabolic and hyperbolic equations that models thermoviscoelastic materials with explicit internal stress relaxation, $$\begin{cases} \tau u_{ttt} + u_{tt} = (D(\Theta)u_{xt})_x + (C(\Theta)u_x)_x, \\ \Theta_t = \Theta_{xx} + |E(\Theta)u_{xt} + F(\Theta)g_t|^2, \\ \tau g_t + g = D(\Theta)u_{xt} + C(\Theta)u_x. \end{cases}$$ The system arises from a stress-strain constitutive relation of Zener type, where the internal variable $g$ encodes mechanical memory effects. A key feature is the explicit coupling of stress relaxation to the heat equation through the dissipation term, which differs from standard approaches that eliminate $g$ via algebraic substitution. Under the assumptions that $\tau>0$ and that $D,C\in C^2([0,\infty))$ are positive and $E,F\in C^1([0,\infty))$, and for suitably regular initial data, we establish local existence and uniqueness of strong solutions. Under additionally strengthened regularity requirements on the initial data and on $D,C$, this solution is moreover shown to be classical. These results extend a corresponding local strong and classical solvability theory developed for the underlying system without the stress variable $g$ to the present, stress-augmented setting.

papers.title: Grushin spherical harmonics in non-degenerate dimension one
papers.abstract: The Grushin Laplacian $\Delta_\alpha = \Delta_x +|x|^{2\alpha}\Delta_y $ is a degenerate elliptic operator in $\mathbb{R}^{h+k}$ that degenerates on $\{0\} \times \mathbb{R}^k$. We explicitly compute the Grushin spherical harmonics on the gauge sphere $\{(x,y) \in \mathbb{R}^{h+k} : |x|^{2(\alpha+1)}+(\alpha+1)^2|y|^2=1\}$ and the corresponding spectrum when the non-degenerate dimension $h=1$, a case not covered by the existing literature. The eigenfunctions consist of homogeneous Grushin-harmonic polynomials of degrees $n \equiv 0,1 \pmod{\alpha+1}$, even and odd in the $x$-variable respectively, which can be described in terms of Jacobi polynomials.

papers.title: Liouville Theorems and Sharp Homogeneity Defects for Weighted Potential Systems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider \[ \begin{cases} u=K*(|x|^\alpha a_0(x)v^p)&\quad\hbox{in }\mathbb R^n,\\ v=K*(|x|^\beta b_0(x)u^q)&\quad\hbox{in }\mathbb R^n, \end{cases} \] where $n\ge2$, $0<\rho<n$, $p,q>0$, and $\alpha,\beta>-\rho$. The radial kernel is nonincreasing and satisfies $K(r)\asymp r^{\rho-n}$. The coefficients satisfy $0<c_0\le a_0(x),b_0(x)\le C_0$ and $|x|(|\nabla\log a_0(x)|+|\nabla\log b_0(x)|)\le L$. We prove nonexistence if \[ \frac{n+\alpha-\varepsilon_a}{p+1} +\frac{n+\beta-\varepsilon_b}{q+1}>n-\rho+\varepsilon_K, \] where the defects bound the radial logarithmic derivatives. No symmetry, finite-energy condition, or prescribed decay is assumed. The proof combines a localized virial identity with a source-layer pressure estimate whose constants are uniform under centered dilations, including the low-order range $0<\rho\le1$. We also identify the necessary scaling range for existence. For radial weighted Newton systems with unequal powers, we prove that the combined coefficient defect has a sharp, unattained infimum equal to the subcritical gap. A fixed bound on the coefficient ratios forces a strictly larger defect, whereas suitable coefficient--solution pairs approach the threshold with excess at most $C/\log M$. In the scalar Newton case, the threshold is explicit and the approximating family converges, after normalization, to an explicit critical weighted profile. The sharpness results concern the Newton kernel; no corresponding construction is asserted for general fractional kernels.

papers.title: Sharp quantitative stability of the Ashbaugh--Benguria inequality
papers.abstract: We establish sharp quantitative stability of the Ashbaugh--Benguria inequality on bounded convex domains in $\mathbb R^n$. After volume and centroid normalization, the eigenvalue-ratio deficit controls the squared $H^{-1/2}(\mathbb S^{n-1})$ norm of the radial displacement from the unit sphere. This yields the optimal exponent $5/2$ for the Fraenkel asymmetry and, for small deficits, the optimal exponent $(n+4)/2$ for the normalized Hausdorff distance. All three exponents are sharp even among smooth strictly convex domains whose principal curvatures lie in $[1/2,2]$. In particular, the quadratic Fraenkel-asymmetry estimate proposed by Brasco and De Philippis (2017, Open Problem 7.65) fails. We also determine the optimal stability exponents under higher-order radial regularity bounds.

papers.title: Sparse power spectrum for passive scalars under Pierrehumbert flow
papers.abstract: We study the long-time Fourier distribution of driven passive scalars transported by an incompressible alternating shear flow (the Pierrehumbert flow) subjected to IID random phase shifts, in the regime of strong shear-strength. With a novel and self-contained proof, we establish (i) a quantitative version of the cumulative Batchelor's law; (ii) quantitative negative regularity mixing estimates; and (iii) a strong form of `sparsity' -- unevenness in the distribution of Fourier mass in radial sectors in frequency space. Our method uses the strong shear-strength assumption to handle a purely deterministic scalar driving term.

papers.title: Chaos of Caputo derivative
papers.abstract: We study bounded realizations of Caputo differentiation on coefficient Banach spaces of fractional power series. The main contribution is an explicit quantitative analysis of local approximation and periodic reconstruction. We determine the least possible simultaneous error in the initial displacement and the prescribed target. The optimal value is attained, and a minimizing perturbation is given explicitly. We also solve the exact-arrival problem and establish uniqueness of its least-norm solution. These formulas provide computable approximation times and identify the sharp threshold for hypercyclicity, mixing and Devaney chaos. Every periodic point is described by a finite block whose geometric repetition yields exact norm formulas. The resulting approximations attain any prescribed sufficiently large minimal period near any given vector. For distinct positive powers, a simultaneous block construction gives quantitative error estimates and the same sharp threshold for disjoint mixing. Compact embeddings relate the Banach realizations to the Mittag-Leffler-Caputo Fr\'echet space. They also exhibit dense stable invariant subspaces inside chaotic realizations. The local approximation condition is a norm formulation of classical transitivity. Its quantitative evaluation, together with explicit periodic and simultaneous reconstruction, provides the central results of the study.
